Subject: Clarify: VPC/on-prem subprocessor matrix, customer keys & data access

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week. We are working through procurement and our security team has a few open items before we can move to an LOI:

1) For Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem option) — can you provide a full list of subprocessors that would have any potential access to customer data (including monitoring, metrics, and backup/recovery providers)? We need the current matrix and a process for notifying/approving new subprocessors.

2) Key control: we need confirmation that we can bring our own keys (Cloud KMS or HSM) and that Redwood cannot derive or escrow keys without explicit contract language.

3) Operator access / break-glass: what conditions allow Redwood staff to access VM disks, logs, or transcript artefacts in private deployments? Are those actions logged and subject to attestation?

4) Cross-border: does Redwood ever route or store customer data outside the US for private deployments? If so, under what legal bases?

Can you send the subprocessor list and a short note on the key/access model? Procurement would like an initial response by EOD Wed so they can schedule a review.

Thanks,
Emma Jones

Emma — thanks for the clear checklist. Looping in Monica (Security / Privacy) and Neha (Legal) to give exact details and the current subprocessor matrix.

Quick summary from my side:
- We support customer-managed keys for both Hosted and Private models (Cloud KMS, customer HSM).
- For Private/VPC: control plane remains under Redwood unless you opt for Private control plane; operator access is restricted by roles and requires documented break-glass approvals.
- Cross-border: by default private deployments keep data in the chosen region; any transfers are explicit and contractually bound.

Subject: Re: Clarify: VPC/on-prem subprocessor matrix, customer keys & data access

Hi Emma — thanks, added detail below and attaching the current subprocessor matrix and a short DPA excerpt that covers Private deployments.

Summary of technical controls (Private / VPC / on-prem):
- Key control:
  * Customer-managed keys (CMKs) supported. For cloud-based Private deployments we integrate with the customer's Cloud KMS (GCP KMS, AWS KMS) or an on-prem HSM via PKCS#11.
  * Envelope encryption: application-level keys are wrapped with CMKs. Redwood never persists unencrypted master keys.
  * Key escrow: Redwood does not escrow customer master keys unless agreed in writing and executed as a separate limited-scope keystore addendum.

- Operator access and emergency procedures:
  * Standard operations: Redwood operator roles get metadata-level visibility (instance health, infra metrics) but not plaintext model inputs/outputs when CMK is active.
  * Break-glass: operator access to disks/logs is possible only under documented break-glass with dual-approval (customer technical contact + Redwood security lead). All actions are logged, stored in an immutable audit trail and surfaced to the customer security console.
  * Attestation: each break-glass event is accompanied by a signed attestation detailing scope, justification, and time window.

- Subprocessors (current snapshot):
  * Cloud infra provider: AWS / GCP (depending on region) — compute, block storage, VPC networking (limited to infra-level; customer data encrypted at rest by CMK).
  * Monitoring/metrics: Prometheus/Managed monitoring partner (no access to decrypted data by default).
  * Backup/DR: third-party snapshot storage (encrypted at rest; keys controlled by customer if CMK option selected).
  * Observability vendor for console (obfuscated traces only).
  * Quantization/compilation partner (model optimization) — no customer PII; limited to model artifacts unless customer explicitly uploads data for tuning.

Process for subprocessors: we operate a 30-day notice window for new subprocessors and provide the matrix + subprocessor SOC summary. Customers can request risk assessments and — for enterprise contracts — we include a right to review and object within 15 days for material changes.

- Cross-border transfers:
  * For Private deployments deployed in a US region, we do not replicate customer data outside the US unless the contract includes an explicit transfer clause (e.g., for global failover).
  * Hosted default: may replicate for availability; Private: customer-controlled.

Attachments: redwood-priv-deploy-subprocessors-20270322.xlsx, redwood-dpa-onprem-key-options-summary.pdf

If you want, we can produce contract language snippets for: (1) CMK-only deployments; (2) break-glass attestation clause; (3) subprocessor notice and objection flow. Happy to join Wed 3pm PT.

—Monica
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Clarify: VPC/on-prem subprocessor matrix, customer keys & data access

Monica — this is helpful, thank you. A few follow-ups and asks from our legal/security: 

1) Please confirm in writing: with CMK enabled, Redwood personnel cannot decrypt data or retrieve plaintext keys. The only allowed exception is the documented break-glass flow with dual approvals and attestation.

2) We need a clear DPA redline for the subprocessor notice + objection flow and a clause that prevents adding subprocessors that would cause data to leave the US without prior written consent.

3) For backup/DR: confirm that snapshots are encrypted with CMK; if we choose customer HSM, we want a technical runbook for key rotation and handling of lost keys.

Attached: our proposed redlines (clearhealth-proposed-redlines.docx) — these track the same items but include binding escrow prohibitions and a narrower break-glass definition.

Can you provide draft contract language by EOD Thu so our counsel can review? We can do Wed 3pm PT as well — that's good.

Thanks,
Emma

Subject: Re: Clarify: VPC/on-prem subprocessor matrix, customer keys & data access

Emma — appreciate the redlines; Neha and I reviewed them this morning. High level: we can accept most of the CMK/attestation language with a few operational clarifications (to avoid blocking critical DR work). Proposed approach:

- Accept: CMK-only deployments where customer holds master key and Redwood cannot derive plaintext. We will add explicit DPA language to state that Redwood will not escrow or copy customer master keys without a separately signed keystore addendum.
- Break-glass: we can agree dual-approval + time-limited access + signed attestation. We propose an SLA-linked post-event report and retention of audit logs for 12 months (extendable).
- Subprocessors: we will include a 30-day notice plus a right to object for material changes. For any subprocessor that would cause cross-border movement we will require written consent.

Trade-offs / ask from Redwood side: for some Private deployment topologies we rely on cloud provider features (e.g., snapshot transport) that could involve subprocessors; we will document those and add a mitigation table.

Next steps: Neha — can you draft the contractual snippets (DPA + SOW appendix + keystore addendum) and I'll sync with Emma after the Wed 3pm call. Emma — DocuSign link to follow once we iterate on language. Attaching a proposed mutual action plan summary.

—Karthik

Attachment: redwood-dpa-onprem-key-options-summary.pdf

FYI forwarding the draft snippets I prepared for RDW-4721. Please review and flag anything you want tightened. Key points included in the doc: 
- "No Escrow" clause: Redwood will not escrow customer master keys unless a separate keystore addendum is executed; any escrow process requires customer explicit written approval and an auditable attestation.
- "Break-glass" definition: explicit conditions, dual approver requirement (customer sec contact + Redwood security lead), access window limited to the incident duration plus 4 hours to collect logs; all steps recorded in immutable audit logs.
- Subprocessor notice: 30-day notice for new subprocessors; 15-day objection window for material changes; contract addendum required if subprocessor causes cross-border transfers.

I'm attaching the draft as a Word doc and a plain text summary. Once you all sign off I'll prepare the DPA redline to send to ClearHealth counsel.
